title: Avoiding states that force a halt
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $K$ work tapes, alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$, and state set $\mathrm{St}$, on a fixed input. Let $X$ be a property of states, and suppose that whenever a configuration is in a state $q$ satisfying $X$, its next step halts and appends the symbol $\beta$ to the current output. If a configuration $c$ has, after $T$ steps, output equal to its initial output followed by a symbol $b\ne\beta$, then at every time $t<T$, any state occupied by the machine fails to satisfy $X$.
